items.title: Part 1: Talking About Yourself Naturally and Completely
items.description: Go beyond yes/no answers by preparing extended responses with reasons, examples, and personal reflections on common Part 1 topics.

items.title: Part 2: Organizing a 2-Minute Response With a Plan
items.description: Learn the structure of a Cue Card response: context, description, why it matters, and what you learned—all within 2 minutes.

items.title: Part 3: Discussing Abstract Concepts and Broader Issues
items.description: Move from personal examples to general statements (In my country, many people..., Nowadays society tends to...) while maintaining coherence.

items.title: Fluency Strategies: Handling Hesitation and Fast Recovery
items.description: Use pause fillers (well, let me think about that, I'd say) naturally; recover from mistakes without losing coherence.

items.title: Pronunciation: Word Stress and Sentence Intonation
items.description: Identify which syllables carry stress in key vocabulary; use intonation to signal questions, contrasts, and emphasis in fluent speech.

items.title: Expressing Opinions and Politely Disagreeing
items.description: Present your views confidently (I believe, From my perspective) and respond to opposing views without being rude or vague.

items.title: Buying Time Techniques: Natural Pauses That Don't Hurt Scores
items.description: Use strategies like rephrasing the question, asking for clarification, and self-correction to gain thinking time without sounding unsure.

items.title: Linking Ideas in Spoken English Naturally
items.description: Connect sentences fluidly with spoken connectors (Well first of all, The thing is, What I mean is) that sound natural, not rehearsed.

items.title: Extending Answers With Depth, Not Just Repetition
items.description: Provide follow-up reasons, personal examples, and alternative viewpoints to transform short answers into band 7+ responses.

items.title: Handling Difficult Topics: Strategies For Unfamiliar Questions
items.description: Respond gracefully to topics you haven't prepared (technology trends, environmental ethics, social media) using universal reasoning skills.

items.title: Eye Contact and Body Language: Projecting Confidence
items.description: Understand the role of non-verbal communication in speaking; maintain engagement with the examiner while managing nerves.

items.title: Accent and Intelligibility: Where to Focus Your Effort
items.description: Distinguish between having an accent (acceptable) and being unintelligible (problematic); prioritize clarity of key vocabulary over perfect pronunciation.
